name: CANOPY SUPER APP
description: Zero-to-one frontend architecture for a Web3 super app — launchpad, DEX, and explorer on a shared interface system.
dossier: Zero-to-one interface architecture for a Web3 super app. Launchpad, DEX, and explorer share one component system so every surface reads as a single operating environment rather than three bolted-on products.
The launchpad had to feel like a control deck: pool state, allocation windows, and wallet status visible without burying the trade path. Navigation is a mission log, not a marketing sitemap.
DEX routing and explorer views inherit the same tokens, density, and motion language. A swap, a contract call, and a block trace all live inside one HUD instead of three visual dialects.
Frontend architecture was treated as infrastructure. Route boundaries, data loaders, and error states were designed before chrome, so the interface could expand without rewriting the cockpit.
Web3 state is hostile to naive rendering. Wallet disconnects, chain switches, and pending transactions are first-class modes, not toast afterthoughts.
The explorer layer turns raw chain noise into readable telemetry: hashes, gas, and confirmations formatted for operators who already know what they are looking for.
Shared primitives — panels, meters, and monospace readouts — keep density high without collapsing into spreadsheet clutter. Every pixel has a job.
The result is a super app that still feels like one machine. New modules dock into the same grid instead of opening a different website.

name: TIMOTHY SYKES
description: Frontend, SEO architecture, and a Cloudflare Workers migration for a high-traffic trading education platform.
dossier: Frontend, SEO architecture, and an edge migration for a high-traffic trading education platform. The brief was simple and brutal: keep the brand loud, make the pages fast, and stop paying latency tax on every lesson.

The marketing surface is a broadcast channel. Hero media, curriculum funnels, and evergreen articles all compete for the first paint. The layout is a split capture: site chrome on one side, proof on the other.
SEO was treated as architecture, not a plugin. Heading order, internal paths, and crawlable lesson indexes were designed so search engines could index the catalog without a second sitemap ceremony.
A Cloudflare Workers migration moved dynamic work to the edge. Origin pressure dropped; cache hits became the default path instead of a lucky exception.
AWS still holds the heavier payloads. The split is deliberate: Workers for request logic, origin for media and durable records. Two machines, one response.
Nuxt owns the view layer. Server routes, meta, and page shells stay typed and predictable while the brand keeps its high-contrast campaign look.
Video and testimonial frames are first-class gallery objects. Scroll the dossier and the capture log advances — lesson stills, broadcast clips, landing variants.
The platform now reads as a live feed instead of a brochure that happens to stream. Traffic spikes no longer feel like a weather event.

name: STOCKS_TO_TRADE
description: Trading education and market data for 1M+ monthly users. Shared Songbird backend with TimothySykes.com: live quotes, catalogs, and publishing.
dossier: StocksToTrade is a high-traffic trading education and market-data platform — charting, scanners, watchlists, webinars, news — for more than a million unique monthly users. TimothySykes.com is the companion education and publishing site for Tim Sykes' content.
Both frontends share one backend I built and own: Songbird. Quotes, news, catalogs, and publishing flow through the same APIs, caches, and pipelines instead of two separate stacks.
I owned frontend and web services for both sites as a full-stack engineer and lead of a four-person team: Nuxt/Vue on Cloudflare, Songbird on AWS, and a shared component library.
I moved them off slow full-site rebuilds onto request-time data — DynamoDB catalogs, S3 JSON, and a shared cache — so pages compose on the request instead of waiting for a rebuild.
Live quotes run over WebSockets. Index feeds, watchlists, and scanners stay current when the tape is loud, with cache windows and fallback snapshots so the HUD does not lie.
Publishing is automated: WordPress ships news and posts to S3, then SSR on the public site. Editorial no longer blocks deploys. AdButler was replaced with our AIZEn ad stack.
I led LLM tooling for QA, SEO integrity checks, and comment moderation. CI/CD and infra — Cloudflare Workers/Pages, AWS deploy, rate limiting — cut a large share of operating cost.
SEO and Core Web Vitals were treated as architecture: JSON-LD, sitemaps, hydration budgets, and cache TTLs. At this traffic, first paint is a product feature.
tasks: Frontend development (news, quotes, charts, Watch Live, lead capture, shared UI)
Real-time market data (WebSockets, quotes, index feeds)
Data engineering (DynamoDB, S3 content, news pipeline)
Performance (SSR, Core Web Vitals, hydration, cache/TTL)
AI / LLM tooling (QA, SEO integrity, comment moderation)
DevOps (Cloudflare Workers/Pages, AWS deploy, CI/CD, rate limiting)

name: HOW TO IMPROVE YOUR WEBSITES PERFORMANCE
description: Practical notes on page load times, Core Web Vitals, and the performance work that actually moves the needle.
dossier: Field notes on page load times, Core Web Vitals, and the performance work that actually moves the needle. No folklore. No 'just add a CDN' as a personality.
LCP is a media problem dressed as a metrics problem. Hero images, fonts, and blocking scripts set the ceiling before your framework ever hydrates.
INP is the human-facing vital. Main-thread congestion, heavy listeners, and layout thrash show up as a UI that feels late even when the network is fine.
CLS is a contract with the layout. Reserve space, don't inject banners after paint, and stop treating web fonts as a surprise guest.
The useful work is boring on purpose: critical CSS, image budgets, cache headers, and killing third-party tags that do not earn their bytes.
Lab scores are a flashlight, not the destination. Field data from real devices decides whether the mission succeeded.
These notes collect the checks I run before calling a page fast: waterfall, filmstrip, and a pass with the network throttled until it hurts.
Performance is a product feature. If the HUD stutters, the operator leaves. The article is a briefing for people who have to ship.
